# Förvaltaren: Kommer spruta ut pengar från bolaget

**Feed**: dagen-med-di  
**Published**: 2026-09-22  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Pareto microcap manager Oscar Karlsson says heavy outflows from small-cap funds have pushed share prices down over the past year, even for companies that beat expectations. In Q2, stocks again rose after good reports, which he sees as an early sign of improving sentiment. He argues earnings growth, net cash and falling valuations will drive returns over time. His main case is Storytel: a profitable subscription model growing at double-digit rates, a P/E of about 13 on next year's earnings and a lot of cash to return to shareholders. He plays down the competitive threat from Spotify, even though Pareto's own analysts cut their Storytel rating in June.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 STORY-B — Storytel | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Guest (Pareto microcap manager): margins went from negative to solidly profitable, P/E ~13 next year, net cash, buybacks and dividends, subscription revenue growing at double digits.

#### Reasoning

Guest's view: the strategic turnaround (pausing expansion into peripheral markets, cost efficiency, operating leverage on ~10% annual growth) has made Storytel a cash cow. Subscription models usually trade at much higher P/Es. Growth in Poland and the Netherlands (Polish prices raised recently) lessens reliance on the Nordics. Host Kalle agrees the turnaround is strong but is unsure about a multiple re-rating. Pareto's own analysts cut their rating in June over Spotify competition.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Spotify competition erodes the Nordic subscriber base or prices
- if growth in Poland/Netherlands stalls
- if margins stop expanding in line with analyst forecasts

> *"Det kommer spruta ut väldigt mycket pengar ur det här bolaget framöver."*
